data.name: Mojtaba
data.gender_notes: Mojtaba is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic root ‘Ajtaba’, meaning ‘to guide or lead’. In the Quran, Allah (SWT) is referred to as Al-Muddaththir, the One Who guides and protects us from the darkness of ignorance and the Fire of Hell. The name Mojtaba carries the meaning “Guided” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Mojtaba usually hope their child will grow to embody guided and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name inspired by the One who guides us on our spiritual journey.
data.etymology: Mojtaba belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Guided.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Mojtaba total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

Context: The period of the Twelve Imams covers the early Islamic history, and Imam Mojtaba is considered as the guide and leader for the Shia community during this time.

Mojtaba bin Seyyed Al-Sharif, was a Persian poet and scholar who lived during the Mongol invasion of Persia in the 13th century. He was known for his resistance against the Mongols and his efforts to preserve Persian culture.
Context: During the Mongol invasion of Persia, Mojtaba played a significant role in trying to resist the invaders and to preserve Persian literature, language, and culture.
